name: Geographic Risk
description: Inherent-risk factors linked to the countries and regions connected to a customer, product or transaction. Covers FATF-listed jurisdictions, secrecy havens, conflict areas, high-corruption environments and trade-diversion hubs.

sources.text: FATF, Guidance for a Risk-Based Approach (sector-specific guidance series, general principles)
FATF Recommendations, Recommendation 1 and Interpretive Note (assessing risks and applying a risk-based approach)
Wolfsberg Group, Guidance on a Risk Based Approach for Managing Money Laundering Risks (2006)

indicators.name: Nexus to FATF black-listed jurisdiction
indicators.desc: Customer, owner or counterparty is connected to a jurisdiction subject to a FATF call for action.
indicators.ctx: Customer, owner or counterparty is connected to a jurisdiction subject to a FATF call for action.
indicators.fp: Humanitarian, diaspora and long-standing commercial links exist.

indicators.name: Nexus to FATF grey-listed jurisdiction
indicators.desc: Connection to a jurisdiction under increased monitoring for strategic deficiencies.
indicators.ctx: Connection to a jurisdiction under increased monitoring for strategic deficiencies.
indicators.fp: Listed jurisdictions change and many controls are improving.

indicators.name: Secrecy or low-transparency jurisdiction
indicators.desc: Entities, accounts or assets are booked in jurisdictions offering strong secrecy or limited transparency, including where unrelated to the entity's operations.
indicators.ctx: Entities, accounts or assets booked in a jurisdiction offering strong secrecy or limited ownership registers.
indicators.fp: Established financial centres host legitimate funds and holdings.

indicators.name: Conflict zone or fragile state exposure
indicators.canon: Conflict zone or fragile state exposure
indicators.desc: Activity involves regions with armed conflict, weak governance or active terrorist groups.
indicators.ctx: Activity involves regions with armed conflict, weak governance or active terrorist groups.
indicators.fp: Aid agencies, journalists and remittance senders operate there lawfully.

indicators.name: High-corruption jurisdiction nexus
indicators.desc: Funds or wealth are linked to or transferred to and from jurisdictions with high perceived corruption.
indicators.ctx: Source of wealth or funds linked to jurisdictions with high perceived corruption.
indicators.fp: Perception indices are broad and many clients are legitimate.

indicators.name: Trade-diversion or transshipment hub
indicators.canon: Routing through trade-diversion or transshipment hubs
indicators.desc: Goods or payments route through third-country hubs or ports with no commercial rationale, or hubs known for rerouting.
indicators.ctx: Flows or goods route through hubs commonly used to reroute goods or avoid restrictions.
indicators.fp: Hubs handle huge volumes of legitimate trade.

indicators.name: Sanctioned country proximity
indicators.desc: Customer or flows are located in or adjacent to comprehensively sanctioned areas.
indicators.ctx: Customer or flows are located in or adjacent to comprehensively sanctioned areas.

indicators.name: Mismatch between customer location and activity geography
indicators.canon: Payments or activity in jurisdictions unrelated to the customer's business or goods
indicators.desc: Payments, counterparties or sales originate in or go to countries with no link to the customer, declared business, services or goods.
indicators.ctx: Transactions concentrate in countries with no link to the customer's residence, business or stated purpose.
indicators.fp: Travel, new suppliers and migration can explain changes.

indicators.name: Offshore financial centre use for non-resident clients
indicators.canon: Offshore financial centre use for non-resident clients
indicators.desc: Funds booked or routed via offshore centres with minimal client ties.
indicators.ctx: Funds booked or routed via offshore centres with minimal client ties.
indicators.fp: Offshore centres serve legitimate wealth planning.

indicators.name: Cross-border corridor with known abuse typologies
indicators.canon: Cross-border corridor with known abuse typologies
indicators.desc: Payments use corridors identified in typology reports as high risk, including regions where informal value transfer is prevalent.
indicators.ctx: Payments to or from corridors identified in public typology reports as high abuse.
indicators.fp: Corridors also carry legitimate migrant remittances.
